title: Add network-dependent smoke tests for remote URL KB sources
sourceOfTruth: gh issue view 136 --json body (Acceptance Criteria, Business Rules, Task Breakdown T-1..T-5)

inventory.producer: scripts/smoke-tests/scenarios/*.sh convention (scenario_state/file_mode in lib/utils.sh; checkSmokeScenarioModes in packages/dev-tools/src/quality-gates/smoke-scenario-modes.ts; is_offline_safe in run-all.sh)
inventory.inputs: the new scenario file's committed git-index mode and its OFFLINE_SAFE= line
consumers: packages/dev-tools smoke-modes:check gate (pre-push + CI build job)
classes: OFFLINE_SAFE=false declared on its own line vs absent/true

inventory.inputs: a reachable HTTPS URL serving a valid KB archive zip + sha256 sidecar
representations: real GitHub release asset (pinned v0.4.3 knowledge-base-0.4.3.zip)
linked dataset under the workspace (.pair/knowledge, .pair/adoption, AGENTS.md, .github, .skills)
consumers: downstream registry install step (apps/pair-cli install pipeline)
classes: clean workspace, no prior cache slot for this URL identity
interactions: AC-2 -> AC-3 (update reuses the identity install established)
AC-2 -> AC-4 (progress evidence is captured from this same install run)

inventory.producer: same chain as AC-2, invoked via `pair update --source <url>` (apps/pair-cli/src/commands/update/handler.ts)
inventory.inputs: a workspace already installed from the same HTTPS URL
representations: re-downloaded archive (customUrl path never short-circuits on cache state, per kb-availability.ts's `if (!deps.customUrl)` guard)

inventory.producer: packages/content-ops/src/http/progress-reporter.ts formatProgress (non-TTY branch) + createProgressReporter/downloadFile (download-manager.ts) — GATED on a `progressWriter` never being threaded from the CLI command layer
inventory.inputs: a download in progress, captured non-TTY (run_pair redirects stdout+stderr to a file, so process.stdout.isTTY is false)
representations: formatProgress non-TTY output: `${label}... ${percentage}% complete\n`, label='Downloading KB' (apps/pair-cli/src/kb-manager/download-manager.ts)
classes: non-TTY progress line present (required) vs the old, non-existent `[N/M] registry-name` format (explicitly ruled out by the AC, and NOT the same as the real, unrelated `[1/7] github ... done` per-registry-copy log line already emitted)
interactions: AC-4 depends on AC-2's install actually invoking the download path

inventory.inputs: a --source value of an unsupported-protocol URL (file://, ftp://) or an arbitrary non-URL string
representations: `Unsupported source protocol: <value>` (kb-availability.ts installFromSource, via detectSourceType returning INVALID)
`KB source path not found: <resolved>` (resolveLocalDataset, for the malformed-string case that falls through to local-path resolution)
classes: malformed non-URL string (falls through to local-path resolution, ENOENT)

inventory.producer: errorHandler.handleHttpError(404,...) (kb-manager/download-manager.ts kbErrorHandler) + isRetryableError (packages/content-ops/src/http/retryable-download.ts) classifying the resulting Error as non-retryable
inventory.inputs: a well-formed HTTPS URL that returns 404
representations: local HTTPS fixture server (self-signed cert, generated at test time) — HTTPS is load-bearing: NodeHttpClientService (packages/content-ops/src/http/http-client-service.ts) dials the `https` module unconditionally; `https.get('http://...')` throws ERR_INVALID_PROTOCOL before any socket opens (verified empirically), so a plain-HTTP fixture (the technical note's `python3 -m http.server` suggestion) would never reach this code path — the AC's own wording already says HTTPS

inventory.producer: isRetryableError + downloadWithRetry's retry loop (packages/content-ops/src/http/retryable-download.ts): DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES=3, DEFAULT_DELAYS=[1000,2000,4000]
inventory.inputs: an HTTPS URL on 127.0.0.1 whose port nothing is listening on (bind-then-immediately-close, so the OS refuses the very next connection deterministically)
representations: ECONNREFUSED network error, classified retryable by RETRYABLE_PATTERNS
total wall-clock duration = attempt(0) + 1s + attempt(1) + 2s + attempt(2) + 4s + attempt(3)-throws >= 7s
classes: connection refused -> retryable -> exhausts the full budget -> fails
interactions: AC-6 and AC-7 share the same isRetryableError producer but land on opposite classes (non-retryable vs retryable)

inventory.producer: is_offline_safe (scripts/smoke-tests/run-all.sh), reading `^OFFLINE_SAFE=` from the scenario file directly — independent of CI_TESTS/CI_EXCLUDED registration
inventory.inputs: `run-all.sh --offline-only` with the new OFFLINE_SAFE=false scenario present on disk
representations: run-all.sh's default (non---ci) scenario loop, gated by is_offline_safe

inventory.producer: scripts/smoke-tests/lib/ci-tests.sh's CI_TESTS/CI_EXCLUDED arrays, audited by scripts/smoke-tests/scenarios/runner-outcomes.sh (CI list integrity, story #400 AC7 as an executable invariant)
inventory.inputs: every `*.sh` file directly under scenarios/ must appear in exactly one of CI_TESTS or CI_EXCLUDED (with a >=20-char reason)
representations: lib/ci-tests.sh CI_EXCLUDED array (not yet touched by this red-spec attempt — config, out of test-only scope)
classes: scenario file exists but is registered in neither array -> UNCOVERED (current state)
scenario registered in CI_EXCLUDED with a network-dependency reason -> covered (post-fix)
interactions: AC-9's oracle (runner-outcomes.sh) also re-validates every OTHER scenario's registration each run — a global invariant, not scoped to this one file

inventory.producer: scripts/smoke-tests/README.md's "Covered Test Scenarios" section (prose; no code producer — the doc's own content is the requirement, so a direct grep against it is the oracle, not an approximation of one)
inventory.inputs: a numbered section documenting remote-source-resolution.sh's name, purpose and exclusion reason, following the `### 8. Agent Harness Functional Smoke` precedent
consumers: a human reading the smoke-suite README instead of ci-tests.sh
classes: scenario undocumented (current state) vs documented with a network-dependency reason (post-fix)
interactions: AC-10's reason text is expected to stay consistent with AC-9's CI_EXCLUDED reason text, though this contract checks only for presence + a network-dependency keyword, not byte-identical wording

fixScope.owner: apps/pair-cli kb-manager remote --source download path + scripts/smoke-tests suite registration

matrix.condition: remote-source-resolution.sh staged in the git index
matrix.expected: reports N tracked scripts staged 100755 (includes remote-source-resolution.sh), exit 0

matrix.condition: the committed scenario file, read directly
clean workspace, network access, pinned HTTPS release-asset URL
matrix.expected: exit 0; .pair/knowledge directory and AGENTS.md present on disk

matrix.condition: workspace already installed from the same HTTPS URL (Test 1's workspace)
the install command from Test 1, captured non-TTY (run_pair redirects to a log file)
matrix.expected: output contains both 'Downloading KB...' and '% complete'
matrix.rationale: Currently absent: no production call site (apps/pair-cli/src/commands/install/handler.ts, update/handler.ts, config/kb-resolver.ts) ever passes a `progressWriter` into resolveDatasetRoot/ensureKBAvailable/installKB, so createProgressReporter (packages/content-ops/src/http/download-manager.ts) always returns undefined and formatProgress is never invoked — verified empirically (2026-09-18): a real `pair install --source <https-release-url>` run prints zero progress lines. Fixing this AC requires a production change threading progressWriter/isTTY from the command layer down; hence fixScope.mode=behavioral, not test.

matrix.expected: exit != 0; output contains 'KB source path not found'

matrix.condition: --source https://127.0.0.1:<ephemeral-port>/missing.zip against a local self-signed-cert HTTPS server that always answers 404, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 for that one child process only
matrix.expected: exit != 0; output contains '404'; elapsed < 5s (no retry delay)
matrix.rationale: Verified empirically that NodeHttpClientService (packages/content-ops/src/http/http-client-service.ts) dials the `https` module unconditionally and throws ERR_INVALID_PROTOCOL synchronously for an http:// URL before any socket opens — a plain-HTTP fixture (the story's Technical-Analysis suggestion of `python3 -m http.server`) would never reach the 404 code path this AC is actually about. The AC's own Given clause already says 'a well-formed HTTPS URL', so the HTTPS fixture follows the authoritative AC text, not the non-binding implementation note.

matrix.condition: --source https://127.0.0.1:<closed-port>/kb.zip where the port was bound then immediately closed (guaranteed refused)
matrix.expected: exit != 0; output contains 'ECONNREFUSED'; elapsed >= 7s (lower bound only)

matrix.condition: remote-source-resolution.sh present on disk with OFFLINE_SAFE=false, run-all.sh invoked with --offline-only (default, non-ci scenario loop)
remote-source-resolution.sh exists under scenarios/ but is registered in neither CI_TESTS nor CI_EXCLUDED (lib/ci-tests.sh untouched by this test-only attempt)
matrix.expected: exit 0 once registered in CI_EXCLUDED with a >=20-char reason naming the network dependency
matrix.rationale: Verified empirically (2026-09-18, via run-all.sh --offline-only which also executes runner-outcomes.sh): fails with 'scenario(s) neither in CI_TESTS nor documented in CI_EXCLUDED: remote-source-resolution.sh'. Fixing this AC means editing scripts/smoke-tests/lib/ci-tests.sh (configuration) — out of this attempt's test-only scope; listed in fixScope.allowedPaths for the implementer.

matrix.condition: scripts/smoke-tests/README.md as it exists today, unedited by this test-only attempt
matrix.expected: README.md contains 'remote-source-resolution.sh' and a case-insensitive mention of 'network'
matrix.rationale: Verified empirically: README.md does not yet mention remote-source-resolution.sh. Fixing this AC means editing scripts/smoke-tests/README.md (docs) — out of this attempt's test-only scope; listed in fixScope.allowedPaths for the implementer. The story's own Testing Strategy for T-5 calls this 'manual read-through' only; this contract makes it executable instead, consistent with the `agent-harness-setup.sh` README precedent this AC is modeled on.

redTests.observed: REPAIR of the rejection's mechanism 'early-exit-blocks-tests-3-9': Test 2's (AC4) two assert_output_contains calls (lines 59-60 of the prior committed script) are now bracketed in set +e/set -e, like the expected-failure blocks already used for Tests 4-8, capturing AC4_RC1/AC4_RC2 into AC4_FAILED instead of a bare `|| exit 1`; AC4_FAILED is re-checked once at the very end of the script (after Test 9) so the overall exit code still reflects a red AC4 even when every later test reaches completion. Reproduced twice at inputHead f1aa6780c58adbbd53cfbb793cb19fef2cdcbef6, network available, real HTTPS release-asset install (v0.4.3) — both runs identical: === Running Remote Source Resolution ===; Test 1 (AC2) PASS: exit 0, .pair/knowledge + AGENTS.md present. Test 2 (AC4) FAIL: "Output does not contain 'Downloading KB...'" and "Output does not contain '% complete'" -- no longer aborts the process. Test 3 (AC3) PASS: exit 0, update succeeded, .pair/knowledge still present. Test 4 (AC5 file://) PASS: exit 1, 'Unsupported source protocol'. Test 5 (AC5 ftp://) PASS: exit 1, 'Unsupported source protocol'. Test 6 (AC5 malformed) PASS: exit 1, 'KB source path not found'. Test 7 (AC6 404) PASS: real 404 from the https-404-server.js fixture ('Error: KB vunknown not found (404)'), exit 1, elapsed 1s < 5s (no retry delay). Test 8 (AC7 retry) PASS: real ECONNREFUSED from the closed-port.js fixture ('connect ECONNREFUSED'), exit 1, elapsed 7s >= 7s (full retry budget). Test 9 (AC10 README) FAIL: README.md does not contain 'remote-source-resolution.sh'. Overall script exit 1 (AC4 and AC10 still red, by design) — all 9 tests ran and asserted in this ONE invocation, closing every closureAssertion in the rejection.
